title: Approximate computation as approximate satisfaction of equality
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a probability space, and let $p$ be a public-coin finite-message protocol with shared randomness in $\Omega$, private inputs from $X$ and $Y$, and outputs in $\alpha$. For every function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ and every real number $\varepsilon$, the assertion that $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ coincides with the assertion that $p$ $\varepsilon$-satisfies the predicate $(x, y, a) \mapsto (a = f\,x\,y)$; that is, the two propositions are equal.
hypotheses_covered: Ω carries a measure space structure
p is a public-coin finite-message protocol over Ω, X, Y, α
f : X → Y → α is an arbitrary function
ε is an arbitrary real number
replaced:
For any protocol $p$, function $f$, and error bound $\varepsilon$,
$p.\mathrm{ApproxComputes}\,f\,\varepsilon = p.\mathrm{ApproxSatisfies}\,(\lambda\,x\,y\,a,\; a = f\,x\,y)\,\varepsilon$.
Thus approximate computation is a special case of approximate predicate satisfaction.
